subject: Cascade request denials from quota controls — urgent customer impact
messages:
From: Matt Robinson <matt.robinson@pulselabmedical.com>

Cc: api-support@pulselabmedical.com
Date: 2026-11-05T15:23:00-08:00
Subject: Repeated 429/500s this week — production traffic blocked

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing a sudden spike in downstream latencies and an elevated rate of 429s and occasional 500s from the Redwood endpoint since Nov 4. This is affecting our patient ingest pipeline — throughput is down ~60% and requests are being rejected mid-stream. Attached is a small sample of logs showing the pattern where a set of user sessions get throttled aggressively for 20-30 minutes.

This started without any announcement on rate changes. We are in a live rollout this week (large inference batches for vitals extraction) and this behavior is causing failed jobs and missed SLAs for hospitals on our platform. Can someone confirm whether a global policy changed or if our account quota got re-applied?

We need an urgent mitigation (temporary capacity bump or bypass) and an explanation of root cause.

Matt Robinson
CTO, PulseLab Medical
matt.robinson@pulselabmedical.com
+1 415-555-0121

Forwarding samples from PLM. Short summary of what I see so far: multiple request streams are being collapsed into a shared enforcement bucket; behaviour looks like policy enforcement is using a conservative burst window and is spilling across routes. This matches a change I noticed in the quota-config-snapshot earlier today.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-06T02:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cascade request denials from quota controls — urgent customer impact

Monica / Kim — quick update from SRE after initial log review: we've identified a misbind in the recent burst-window rollout that inadvertently collapsed multiple route groups into a single enforcement key. The effect: short, high-concurrency bursts from PLM are being applied against a shared burst budget rather than the per-route budget, causing sequential spillover and extended rejections (20-40m observed).

Root cause: a config templating change (rolled out 2026-11-04 22:40 UTC) that changed the enforcement key from route+customer -> route-only in a subset of nodes. This was meant to improve efficiency for low-cardinality tenants but had an unintended grouping effect.

Immediate mitigations completed (11/06 02:00 UTC):
- Rolled back the templated change to enforcement key logic on the affected nodes.
- Applied a temporary per-customer burst override for PulseLab (PLM) to recover throughput while we validate.
- Added a short-term frequency cap exemption for their dedicated pool for the next 6 hours.

Next steps:
1) Full rollout of rollback across all regions (in progress).
2) Postmortem and fixed test covering enforcement-key permutations.
3) Proposal to add synthetic tests simulating concurrent session bursts for top-30 tenants.

Can we get exec approval for a one-off credit (billing) and a brief customer SLO concession while we finish validation? I'll attach the rollout timeline and verification checks to the postmortem.

Karthik Iyer
Director, SRE — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
